topic: How do distributed satellite constellations impact orbital configuration trade-offs between coverage and inter-satellite interference mitigation?
consensus_response: Dense satellite constellations increase inter-satellite interference, directly impacting network capacity and necessitating advanced mitigation techniques like adaptive beamforming and space-time coding. This interference arises from signal overlap and reduced frequency availability, directly impacting network capacity.  Proper orbital configuration management, considering propagation models and signal path interference, is critical for achieving optimal coverage and minimizing interference.  Effective mitigation techniques like adaptive antenna pointing and advanced signal processing schemes are crucial to ensure robust coverage in dense constellations.
